basis: Craniofacial dysostosis, ocular malformations and cleft lip/palate define disease; encephalocele and olfactory-tract hypoplasia occur in 30-79%.
Retinal rod-cone degeneration; scoliosis reported in 1/2 patients (50%) supports skeletal involvement, although the sample is small.
Iron-metabolism disorder with anemia and neurodegeneration; retinal degeneration occurs in 30-79%; hepatic iron deposition alone does not establish liver dysfunction.
Sulfite-metabolism defect causes severe encephalopathy; ectopia lentis is characteristic and occurs in roughly half of surviving patients.
Craniosynostosis is premature fusion of cranial bone sutures; no additional organ involvement is established.
Cerebellar disease and axonal neuropathy define SCA43; pectus carinatum occurs in 4/7 and pes cavus in 30-79%, supporting skeletal involvement.
Cowpox virus infection produces localized cutaneous lesions in humans.
Congenital urachal remnant cyst belongs to the urinary system; infection and other complications occur in a minority.
Inherited cone-rod retinal degeneration with macular atrophy and visual dysfunction.
Aniridia, microcornea and cataract are defining structural abnormalities of the eye.
Inherited triglyceride storage disorder; skeletal myopathy occurs commonly across both major types (>30%); skin and cardiac involvement vary by subtype.
Neurodevelopmental impairment is common: developmental delay 16/21 and microcephaly 14/21; functional ocular, cardiac, renal and hearing defects are individually uncommon.
Primary skeletal-muscle dystrophy; common white-matter MRI changes alone do not establish functional neurologic damage; symptomatic neurologic disease is variable.
Respiratory-chain defect with progressive encephalopathy; muscle dysfunction with COX-negative fibers in 15/15; optic atrophy in 2/2. Respiratory failure may be neuromuscular.
Congenital muscle disease and bone fractures define the syndrome; obstructive sleep apnea in 3/3 supports common upper-airway dysfunction.
Structural narrowing of the gastric pylorus causes gastric outlet obstruction.
Carcinoma originates in breast tissue, which has no axis; lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates do not make it lymphoma or an immune-mediated disease.
Congenital absence of nasal bones is a skeletal malformation; nasal shape alone does not establish airway dysfunction.
Peripheral nerve-sheath neoplasm usually presenting in skin or subcutis; uncommon visceral sites do not apply across the umbrella.
Cartilage-producing neoplasms predominantly arise in skeletal tissues; representative diseases include osteochondroma, chondroblastoma and chondrosarcoma.
KSHV-driven cytokine inflammation commonly causes anemia and thrombocytopenia (>80% in reported cohorts); associated Kaposi sarcoma and lymphoma are separate diseases.
Macular retinal dysfunction causes progressive bilateral visual loss despite a normal-appearing fundus.
Generalized epilepsy defines the disease; ictal mouth and eye movements do not establish gastrointestinal or ocular damage.
Syndromic neurodevelopmental disease; bilateral ptosis occurs in 30-79%; constipation alone does not establish bowel injury; supplied cardiac lesions are individually <30%.
Infantile epilepsy is a neurologic disorder despite its usually self-limited course; no additional organ damage is established.
